arrival.content:
The date consistency check is still flagging the last three cores from the 2026-04-02 rebuild as "verified," but I’ve been staring at CM-188 for the last hour and the two-layer hypothesis is holding up against the slump model, which worries me more than the data supports. If it’s a doublet, the recurrence interval drops by forty percent, and if it’s a slump, we’ve got a structural artifact that’s been masquerading as a signal since we started logging.

Wren hasn’t eaten since yesterday morning. I’m not going to ask her if she’s hungry again. I’m going to leave a sandwich on the bench next to the core scanner and tell her to look at the grain-size distribution in layer 4 of CM-188 before she touches the lab notebook. If she ignores the food, she’ll miss the shift in the median. If she ignores the median, she’ll call it a slump.

I need to know which one it is. I need to know before the radiocarbon dates come back, because if I send those samples to the lab thinking it’s a single event and it’s two, we’ve just wasted six weeks and a budget line item that won’t come back until next year.

I’m going to run the depth check again, but this time I’m going to inject a fake offset into the depth sensor data for CM-188 just to make sure the algorithm catches it. If it doesn’t, I’m tearing the script apart. I don’t trust it until it breaks.

gate.content:
I can’t put that in the abstract.

I know you can see it. I know you’ve been looking at those cores for twenty years and your eyes are sharper than my algorithms. But I also know that CM-188 is the only core in the entire transect showing a doublet, and every other core shows a single event. That is not a pattern; that is an outlier. And outliers are where the slump hides.

If we publish that as a confirmed doublet without ruling out the slump, and it turns out to be a slump, the paper is wrong. If it’s wrong, the recurrence interval is wrong. If the recurrence interval is wrong, the risk models for the coast are wrong. And if the risk models are wrong, people die.

You want it in the abstract by Friday. I can get you the grain-size distribution for layer 4 by tomorrow morning. I can get you the median shift. I can get you the proof that it’s not a single event. But I will not get you the confirmation that it’s two earthquakes until I have ruled out the slump.

I’m going to run the depth check on CM-188 again, but this time I’m going to break it. I’m going to inject a fake offset and make sure the script catches it. If it doesn’t, I’m tearing the code apart. I don’t trust it until it fails.

Eat the sandwich. I left it on the bench. If you skip it, you’ll miss the shift in the median. And if you miss the shift, you’ll call it a slump.

I’m not saying it’s a slump. I’m saying I don’t know yet. And I need to know before Friday.
